narration.text: Halve the Moon's distance, tides grow eightfold.
Tidal pull scales with the cube of distance.
Today the Moon averages 384,399 kilometres away.
Its distance already swings between 357,000 and 407,000 kilometres.
Halving it would be a jump no orbit ever gives.
The next high tide, about 12 hours later, would arrive enormous.
And the Moon would look twice as wide.
So Earth would notice within a single tide.
